items.explanation: Shows the planner's chosen plan and estimated costs without running.
items.example: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 'ALFKI';
items.expected: Plan lines (e.g. Seq Scan or Index Scan).

items.explanation: Runs the query and reports actual rows and timing; wrap writes in a transaction.
items.example: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM order_details WHERE quantity > 10;
items.expected: Plan lines with actual time and rows.

items.explanation: Speeds up selective WHERE, JOIN and ORDER BY on col; costs space and write time.
items.example: CREATE INDEX tmp_orders_customer ON orders (customer_id); SELECT indexname FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'orders';
items.expected: Index list for orders including tmp_orders_customer (rolled back).

items.explanation: Usable for filters on a, or a and b; leading column matters.
items.example: CREATE INDEX tmp_od_prod_qty ON order_details (product_id, quantity); EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM order_details WHERE product_id = 11 AND quantity > 5;
items.expected: Plan for the query (may still choose a seq scan on tiny tables).

items.syntax: WHERE d >= x AND d < y  (not WHERE f(d) = …)
items.explanation: Functions on the column block plain indexes; rewrite as a range or use an expression index.
items.example: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_date >= (SELECT MIN(order_date) FROM orders) AND order_date < (SELECT MIN(order_date) FROM orders) + interval '1 year';
items.expected: One row: orders in the first year of data.

items.explanation: EXISTS stops at the first match.
items.example: SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.freight > 100) LIMIT 5;
items.expected: Customers with at least one high-freight order.

items.syntax: SELECT a, b instead of SELECT *
items.example: SELECT order_id, order_date FROM orders ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 5;

items.syntax: JOIN (SELECT k, SUM(x) … GROUP BY k) t
items.explanation: Shrinks rows before an expensive join and avoids fan-out.
items.example: SELECT c.company_name, t.orders FROM customers c JOIN (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) t USING (customer_id) ORDER BY t.orders DESC LIMIT 5;

items.explanation: Updates planner statistics after big data changes.
items.example: ANALYZE orders; SELECT relname, n_live_tup FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE relname = 'orders';
items.expected: Row with live tuple count for orders.

items.syntax: WHERE id > :last_id ORDER BY id LIMIT n
items.explanation: Avoids scanning skipped rows that OFFSET still reads.
items.example: SELECT order_id, order_date FROM orders WHERE order_id > 50 ORDER BY order_id LIMIT 5;
